content: 1. Intensive Group Learning in Liberia: A study by James S. Urey, R. Greifinger, D. Lloyd, and others evaluated the impact of intensive group learning and on-site services on improving sexual and reproductive health among young adults in Liberia. This randomized evaluation, published in Global Health Science and Practice in 2016, highlighted the effectiveness of the Healthy Actions program in addressing these health concerns. 2. HIV Prevention in Drug Courts: Festinger DS, Dugosh KL, Kurth AE, and Metzger DS examined the efficacy of a computer-facilitated HIV prevention tool within drug court settings. Their findings, published in Drug and Alcohol Dependence in 2016, demonstrated the potential of technology-based interventions in reducing HIV risk behaviors among individuals in the criminal justice system. 3. HIV Testing Campaign for African American Women: Uhrig JD, Davis KC, Fraze J, Goetz J, and Rupert D assessed the effectiveness of an HIV testing campaign targeting African American women. Published in Health Marketing Quarterly in 2012, the study emphasized the importance of tailored messaging to encourage HIV testing in this population. 4. Reducing Stigma and Increasing HIV Testing in Malawi: Derksen L, Muula A, Oosterhout J, Lettow M, Matengeni A, and Sodhi S conducted a cluster-randomized trial in Malawi to evaluate a health information intervention aimed at reducing stigma and increasing HIV testing. Their findings, published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2015, highlighted the intervention's success in improving testing rates. 5. Message Framing to Motivate HIV Testing: Apanovitch AM, McCarthy D, and Salovey P explored the use of message framing to encourage HIV testing among low-income, ethnic minority women. Their research, published in Health Psychology in 2003, demonstrated the effectiveness of strategic communication in motivating health behaviors. 6. Online HIV Prevention for MSM: Mikolajczak J, Van Breukelen GJ, and Kok G evaluated an online HIV prevention intervention designed to promote HIV testing among men who have sex with men (MSM). This randomized controlled trial, published in the Netherlands Journal of Psychology in 2012, showed promising results in increasing testing rates within this population. 7. HIV Risk Reduction Counseling in South Africa: Simbayi LC, Kalichman SC, Skinner D, Jooste S, Cain D, Cherry C, and colleagues implemented theory-based HIV risk reduction counseling for sexually transmitted infection (STI) clinic patients in Cape Town, South Africa. Their study, published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2004, demonstrated the intervention's effectiveness in reducing risky sexual behaviors. 8. Improving HIV Rapid Testing Rates in STD Clinics: Carey MP, Coury-Doniger P, Senn TE, Vanable PA, and Urban MA conducted a randomized controlled trial to improve HIV rapid testing rates among STD clinic patients. Published in Health Psychology in 2008, the study highlighted strategies to increase testing uptake in clinical settings. 9. Their findings, published in AIDS Care in 2010, underscored the importance of counseling in improving adherence and follow-up rates. 10. HIV Testing and Risk Reduction in Buprenorphine Treatment: Edelman EJ, Moore BA, Caffrey S, Sikkema KJ, Jones ES, Schottenfeld RS, and others examined the integration of HIV testing and sexual risk reduction counseling in office-based buprenorphine/naloxone treatment. Published in the Journal of Addiction Medicine in 2013, the study demonstrated the feasibility and benefits of incorporating HIV prevention into addiction treatment. 11. Single-Session HIV Prevention for Black Women: Diallo DD, Moore TW, Ngalame PM, White LD, Herbst JH, and Painter TM conducted a group randomized controlled trial to assess the efficacy of a single-session HIV prevention intervention for Black women. Published in AIDS Behavior in 2010, the study highlighted the intervention's success in reducing HIV risk behaviors. 12. Rapid HIV and Hepatitis C Screening in Emergency Departments: Merchant RC, DeLong AK, Liu T, and Baird JR identified factors influencing the uptake of rapid HIV and hepatitis C screening among drug-misusing adults in emergency departments. Their findings, published in AIDS Behavior in 2015, provided insights for designing future screening interventions. 13. Culturally Tailored HIV Risk-Reduction Messages: Kalichman SC, Kelly JA, Hunter TL, Murphy DA, and Tyler R developed culturally tailored HIV/AIDS risk-reduction messages for African-American urban women. Published in the Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology in 1993, the study demonstrated the impact of culturally sensitive messaging on risk awareness and behavior change. 14. Enhancing HIV Testing Messages for African American Women: Kalichman SC and Coley B explored the use of context framing to enhance HIV-antibody testing messages targeted at African American women. Their research, published in Health Psychology in 1995, emphasized the importance of framing in improving testing uptake. 15. HIV Prevention App for Urban Youth: Cordova D evaluated the preliminary efficacy of an HIV prevention intervention app in an urban youth-centered community health clinic. Published in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 2018, the study highlighted the potential of digital tools in engaging youth in HIV prevention. 16. Women’s Experiences with HIV Counseling and Testing: Exner TM, Hoffman S, Parikh K, Leu C-S, and Ehrhardt AA explored women’s experiences with HIV counseling and testing and the perceived role of testing as a prevention strategy. Published in Perspectives on Sexual and Reproductive Health in 2002, the study provided valuable insights into the barriers and facilitators of HIV testing among women. 17. WHO Guidelines on HIV Testing Services (2019): The guidelines also highlighted the importance of concise post-test counseling messages tailored to specific populations and their test results, as well as the need for effective linkage to prevention, care, and support services.
